title: Fleet Pilot: scaling dials, throughput explorer, and edit history
creator: Sofia Morales
description: Build an integrated Fleet Controls panel (’Fleet Pilot’) that lets operators: 1) adjust scaling targets via compact interactive controls (scaling dials and quick-presets), 2) explore recent and historical throughput/latency trends in an interactive throughput explorer, and 3) view and act on a tamper-proof change history with diff/rollback capabilities. Goal: provide an operator-first view for Dedicated customers to tune throughput guarantees and autoscaling policies without requiring CLI/Git changes. Scope covers frontend Console UI, backend APIs for control changes, audit-log plumbing that writes immutable events to the existing audit store, and lightweight safe-apply semantics with quick rollback. Excludes policy engine rewrite; we will call existing autoscale APIs and the capacity planner service.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can change target RPS and burst buffer using the scaling dials; changes are applied via the safe-apply endpoint and return a 200 with job id
Throughput Explorer shows 7d/30d/90d selectable windows with percentile lines (p50/p95) and request-level heatmap tied to model/version
Every change appears in the Change History table with user, timestamp, before/after, and optional reason; entries include links to the commit-like job id
Rollbacks can be initiated from a change entry and will trigger a controlled reapply using the previous manifest within 3 minutes and surface progress in the UI
RBAC respects existing role mappings: only users with fleet.operator or fleet.admin can make scaling edits; read-only users see explorer and history
Telemetry: each control change emits events to telemetry pipeline with tags for customer_id, fleet_id, actor, and delta; dashboards ingest these events within 5 minutes
E2E smoke tests validate UI->API path and history entry creation; coverage included in console-acceptance-suite
comments: 2025-02-14 Sofia Morales: Kickoff — scoped MVP to dials + throughput explorer + immutable change history. Flagged risks around audit-store throughput; opened ENG-20987 for audit-store write optimization.

2025-02-19 Aisha Patel: UX wireframes uploaded to Figma (see attachment). We decided to favor compact dials + quick-presets over full numeric fields to reduce operator hesitation. PM/Design review approved.

2025-02-23 Ethan Wu (Eng): Backend sketch — will expose /fleets/{id}/scaling/safe-apply that performs validation, writes audit event, and queues a reconcile job. Estimate 3 backend days + 2 infra days for audit-store tuning (ENG-20234).

2025-02-27 Design review: Added a 'preview impact' panel that simulates expected token/sec and estimated cost delta. Decision: use historical traffic profile sampling for simulation rather than model-based estimate to reduce complexity.

2025-03-02 QA: Created exploratory test plan for rollbacks; found race where two rapid edits can create conflicting jobs. Mitigation: job dedup and optimistic lock in safe-apply (ENG-21455 scheduled).
2025-03-05 Sofia Morales: Product review — ready for feature branch merge; coordinated release window with infra team for audit-store migration to partitioned writes (planned 2025-03-18).
2025-03-05 Link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4127 (WIP — frontend), backend PR queued https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/2893
notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) Full policy editor vs quick controls — chose quick controls to lower cognitive load and speed up ops. 2) Simulation accuracy vs latency — use sampled historical traffic for immediate feedback. Operational constraint: audit-store throughput must support peak write bursts when multiple fleets are updated; ENG-20987 must land before GA.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): UI dials + throughput explorer + audit write (safe-apply) -> internal dogfood on two enterprise customers. Phase 2: add canary rollouts and autoscale policy presets + operator presets sync. Phase 3: integrate cost-optimization suggestions from Optimize service.
risks: Audit-store write contention under large enterprise churn
Race conditions for concurrent edits leading to oscillation
Misleading simulation results if historical profile changes rapidly
